newsitem.title: USA: ITT TO SELL SHARE IN KNICKS, RANGERS, MADISON SQUARE GARDEN. [CORRECTED 04:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ITT TO SELL SHARE IN KNICKS, RANGERS, MADISON SQUARE GARDEN. [CORRECTED 04:10 GMT]

text.p: ITT Corp. said Thursday it would sell its half interest in New York's Madison Square Garden, the NBA's Knicks, the NHL's Rangers and the MSG cable television network to its partner Cablevision Systems Corp. for $650 million.

ITT, which is fending off a hostile $6.5 billion takeover bid from Hilton Hotels Corp., said the deal puts a value on the arena, professional basketball and hockey teams and associated properties at $1.53 billion.
"The Madison Square Garden properties remain core strategic assets for Cablevision," Cablevision Chief Executive Officer James Dolan (corrects from chairman Charles Dolan) said in a statement.

"We are committed to operating the Garden in a manner that produces winning treams and increased opportunities for New York area residents to enjoy sports and entertainment events, in person and on television.
"Cablevision is also committed to providing continued support for the excellent management team in place at the Garden."
The sale of the arena by ITT was seen as the latest step in the New York-based hotel and casino company's defence against Hilton's takeover offer.
Cablevision, which teamed up with ITT in 1995 to buy the famous arena, had been seen as the top candidate to acquire the stake from ITT.
ITT, which also owns the Sheraton hotel chain and Caesars casinos, said the deal would give it an 81 percent gain in just two years over its original net investment of $360 million.
"This has been an extremely successful investment for ITT over the past two years," ITT Chairman Rand Araskog said in a statement.
Under the deal, Cablevision initially will pay ITT $500 million in cash for a 38.5 percent stake in Madison Square Garden.
ITT also has the option to require Woodbury, New York-based Cablevision to purchase half of the remaining stake in the arena for $150 million in the two years following the closing of the deal.
Cablevision is the sixth largest U.S. operator of cable television systems.
